messages:
arjun: Heads-up — I'm proposing an 'access filtration' prefilter in the Console control plane. Short pitch: push easy auth + tenant predicates before fanout to query layer to cut cost/latency on common dashboard views. RFC gist: https://go/rfc-access-filtration (draft)

sarah: curious — how different from the existing prefilter? we already have some auth prechecks in the gateway.

arjun: good q. Current gateway checks token + coarse tenancy but still fans out to many shards. Filtration applies a lightweight predicate layer (indexed keys, time windows) that can prune rows per-tenant early. Key tradeoff: we may return slightly different counts for edge rollups unless we coordinate eviction/caching.

mike: worried about correctness for analytics tiles. if filtration prunes before aggregation we could undercount.

arjun: agreed — plan is: only filter on deterministic tenant-scoped predicates (resource id lists, tenant_id, time_range) that are safe before aggregation. For rolls/approx counts we route to slowpath which runs full query. Default is fastpath with filtration + cached projection.

jen: can we see a config sketch? how would routes opt into fastpath vs slowpath?

arjun: pasted sketch:
```
# console.controlplane.filters
- route: /dash/*/tiles
  fastpath: true
  predicates:
    - tenant_eq: tenant_id
    - indexed_in: widget_id
  slowpath_fallback: policy("always_on_error")
```

kal: latency numbers? batching effects?

arjun: in perf testing: fastpath reduced mean p95 by ~120ms for small tiles and cut queries to DB by 40%. Overhead of prefilter is tiny (<5ms) but it changes caching semantics — cache keys need to include filtered predicate signature.

sarah: important: auth decisions must be auditable. We need logs and an attachable trace id when we short-circuit.

arjun: yep — plan to emit `access.filter.trace` events with reason codes. example: `FILTERED:indexed_mismatch` or `SLOWPATH:aggregation_required`.

mike: ops concern: rollout plan?

arjun: phased feature flag: start with internal dashboards -> opt-in teams -> perf experiments -> org-wide. We'll ship metrics and a regression guard: if tile accuracy deviate > 0.2% vs slowpath we auto-disable for that route.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: control-plane/filters v0.1 -> canary on prod-1 @ 2026-06-10T03:00Z

jen: ack. I'll file a follow-up to map which tiles are safe for fastpath. also need a short RFC followup doc with example queries to verify correctness.

sarah: +1. add security review for KMS of logs if needed.

arjun: thanks — I'll post the RFC follow-up with test harness and a small compatibility shim to preserve existing cache keys until cutover.

mike: thanks. Ping me when you have canary metrics; I'll run load test.

jen: noted. I'll coordinate with platform on rollout checklist.

arjun: cool — next sync Friday 10am PT. tl;dr: access-filtration fastpath to lower cost/latency, slowpath for correctness, phased rollout + metrics gates. :rocket:
